<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **15** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2808069121307b05d466b02ee415b3fa9a09a06d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `66837c080256430e126d5938fdd167a30794e395` — the merge of head `3f7b18399ae2841b79fd299eafade906651cdd7c` into base `2808069121307b05d466b02ee415b3fa9a09a06d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 66837c080256430e126d5938fdd167a30794e395 && git checkout 66837c080256430e126d5938fdd167a30794e395
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2808069121307b05d466b02ee415b3fa9a09a06d 3f7b18399ae2841b79fd299eafade906651cdd7c && git checkout -B drift-repro 2808069121307b05d466b02ee415b3fa9a09a06d && git merge --no-ff 3f7b18399ae2841b79fd299eafade906651cdd7c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2808069121307b05d466b02ee415b3fa9a09a06d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 2808069121307b05d466b02ee415b3fa9a09a06d` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `3f7b18399ae2841b79fd299eafade906651cdd7c`
Local-runs: none

PR #23309 (draft, `needs:contract-review`, auto-merge unarmed, no reviews) for card #23254. The head is the merge of `859822b51` with `origin/main` `543b33dee`; the net diff against that merge base is 4 files, +306 / −1, equal to the PR's file list (`auth-plugin.ts` +47/−1, `organization-record-page-option.test.ts` +218, `README.md` +27, one changeset +14). Read: the card body and all four comments (triage `6146018242`, claim `6147450905`, os-dev-report `6151220182`; the seat ACCEPT `6151254191` is not taken as evidence), ruling A `6134056653`, the PR body, its one bot comment (docs drift, advisory), the GitHub diff and file list, the head's check-runs, and the head by sha in read-only git. PR #23206 as landed on `main` (the registry doors in `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts`, its changeset, migration entry 18) read for the refusal and its remedy text.

### ① Derived judgments

**(a) Within ruling A; the option is a sound published contract.** The diff adds one optional key, `AuthPluginOptions.registerOrganizationRecordPage?: boolean` (`@default true`), read once in `init()` as `this.options.registerOrganizationRecordPage !== false`, and one conditional on the `pages:` list of the existing `manifest.register` call. No precedence ladder, no registration-order rule, no served field, no change to the registry's two refusal doors (`refuseDefaultRecordPageConflicts`, `registerItem`), to `defaultRecordPageObject`, or to the save door. The default is unchanged by construction: the constructor spreads the caller's options over `{ registerRoutes: true, basePath }`, so an absent key and an explicit `undefined` both read `!== false` → the page is kept; only a literal `false` removes it. Name and polarity: it is a mechanism name (what plugin-auth does), default-true with `false` as the opt-out, the same shape as `registerRoutes` on the same interface, in `camelCase` as the naming rule asks, with no env var or setting behind it. For the AI-authoring axis the mechanism spelling is the right one: a host declaration (`hostOrganizationRecordPage: true`, the `hostSignInHandoff` shape) would assert a fact the runtime never checks, which is the declared-but-unenforced shape Prime Directive #10 refuses; `registerOrganizationRecordPage: false` states exactly what the runtime does and the pins prove it. An agent diagnosing the refusal reaches it: the refusal names the holder (`com.objectstack.plugin-auth` / `sys_organization_detail`), and the TSDoc, README and changeset each name `DEFAULT_RECORD_PAGE_CONFLICT` beside the option, so a grep on the code or the page lands on the remedy. The one thing a mechanism name does not say — that a host may set `false` with no page of its own — is stated in the TSDoc, the README and the boot line (synthesized default layout, no tab strip).

**(b) Exactly one registration removed; nothing dangles — verified at the sha.** The `manifest.register` call still spreads `authIdentityManifest(...)` (objects, objectExtensions), registers `dashboards: [SystemOverviewDashboard]`, `datasets`, the conditional `nav_sso_providers` contribution, and `SysUserDetailPage` on every path; `registerRoutes`, the `auth` and `tenancy` services are untouched. `manifest.ts` declares no page list (`AUTH_PLUGIN_ID` and the identity manifest only) and `identity-objects-plugin.ts` registers objects only, so the dev's "not touched" deviation is correct. `git grep sys_organization_detail` at the head outside plugin-auth hits only: the page's own definition (`platform-objects/src/pages/sys-organization.page.ts`, `isDefault: true`, slotted, three `record:related_list` tabs Members / Invitations / Teams); the `pages.sys_organization_detail.label` bundle entries in the four locale files and three source-hash files (keyed by page name, read only when a page of that name is served — no runtime parity check exists between registered pages and bundle keys: `check-app-nav-i18n.mjs` dropped its pages verdict under #15743 and names the page in a comment only); `platform-page-i18n-parity.test.ts`, which reads its population from the `@objectstack/platform-objects/pages` barrel and the served bundles without a kernel boot (the barrel still ships the page); `i18n-extract.config.ts` and `check-i18n-coverage.mjs` (comments only); `platform-objects/CHANGELOG.md`; one QA checklist item. The shipped console (`packages/console/dist`) has zero occurrences. No code under `packages/metadata-protocol`, `packages/rest`, `packages/cli/src` or any Studio surface names the page or resolves "the default record page of object X" and fails on absence; `os validate` enforces the one-default rule stack-locally in `defineStack` (`stack.zod.ts`) and never sees plugin-auth's page. The Setup nav reaches the organization record view by object plus templated `recordId` (ADR-0133 D3, `nav_organization`), never by page name, and ADR-0133 D3 states the tab set is declared by the page record, not the ADR, so no ADR binds plugin-auth to register it unconditionally (ADR-0005, ADR-0086 and ADR-0133 read).

**(c) The three pins are triage's, each with a control, on a real kernel.** Harness: a real `ObjectKernel` (`@objectstack/core`), the real `ObjectQLPlugin`, `SqlDriver` on in-memory better-sqlite3 (`@objectstack/driver-sql`, a declared devDependency), `AuthPlugin` from source, and a host plugin depending on `com.objectstack.engine.objectql` that registers its own `isDefault: true` record page through the `manifest` service in `init()` — the same shape as the package's `identity-objects-plugin.test.ts`. The refusal is thrown by `SchemaRegistry.registerItem`'s seam (registry.ts, the ADR-0112 envelope); nothing is mocked. Pin 1 (`false`, both orders): `sys_organization`'s defaults are exactly the host page, `sys_organization_detail` is absent from plugin-auth's registered pages, `sys_user_detail` unchanged; control = pin 3. Pin 2 (no option): defaults are exactly plugin-auth's page; control: `false` with no host page gives `[]`, so the reading is not vacuous. Pin 3 (both pages, no option, both orders): `code` + `status 422`, `object`, and the `incoming` / `existing` pair, which flips with order — that is the no-order-rule pin: whichever page is second is refused; control: explicit `true` refused the same way. Ablation (dev's reading, consistent with the pins' construction): making registration unconditional reds pin 1 and pin 2's control and leaves pin 3 green, which is right — pin 3 pins the unchanged default and the #23206 door, and the regression it catches is a polarity flip (`=== true` would boot the no-option composition and red pins 2 and 3). Pin 3 is therefore meaningfully protected. Minor gap, non-blocking: an explicit `undefined` key is argued in the PR body but not pinned (absent, `false` and `true` are); the `!== false` read and the spread constructor make it correct by reading.

**(d) The `info` line is appropriate and not noisy.** One line, only when `false`, emitted once in `init()` beside the existing `Auth Plugin initialized successfully` line, naming the option, what is not registered, and what a host without its own page then sees. It is a chosen composition, not a degradation, so `info` rather than `warn` is the level the degradation-log rule gives (a screen deliberately absent, visibly smaller, nothing claimed-persisted lost), and it satisfies "absence must be loud, naming the remedy". It carries no tracker number (the runtime-string rule). Not pinned, as prose; no rule asks for a pin on log prose.

**(e)** in ②. **(f)** in ③.

**(g) CI on the head** (check-runs read at 2026-10-13T17:32Z; 43 runs): 30 `success`, including `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset` (both runs), `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, every `Lint ·` job, `Test Core (5/6)` and `Test Core (6/6)`. Non-green at read time — `in_progress` (4): `Test Core (1/6)`, `Test Core (2/6)`, `Test Core (3/6)`, `Test Core (4/6)`. `skipped` (9, path-filtered, opt-in or full-battery jobs that do not run on a PR): `Auto Label` (second run), `Build Docs`, `Check PR Size` (second run), `Console Pin Gate`, the Dogfood Regression Gate matrix shard job (its check-run name carries an unexpanded matrix template token), `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)` (both runs), `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`. No run is `failure`. The landing waits for the four Test Core shards; this record does not vouch for them.

### ② Semver level

`'@objectstack/plugin-auth': minor` with `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is correct. Pre mode is on (`.changeset/pre.json`: mode `pre`, tag `next`; plugin-auth at `18.0.0-next.0`), so the bump lands as the next `18.0.0-next.N`; `minor` is the floor Clause-② `yes` takes, and `(widening)` is the right arm of the closed pair: a new optional key, nothing narrowed. The changeset, sentence by sentence against the head: "at most one `isDefault: true` record page per object ... refused at registration with `DEFAULT_RECORD_PAGE_CONFLICT`" — the registry doors of PR #23206, 422. "`AuthPlugin` always registered `sys_organization_detail` (the Members / Invitations / Teams tab strip) as the default record page of `sys_organization`" — `pages: [SysOrganizationDetailPage, SysUserDetailPage]` on `main`, the page `isDefault: true` with those three tabs. "refused at boot" — pin 3. "defaults to `true`. Only an explicit `false` leaves out ... whichever plugin starts first. Plugin order and precedence rules play no part" — the `!== false` read, pin 1 in both orders. "still registers the identity objects, the `sys_user_detail` record page, the System Overview dashboard, and the auth routes and services" — all in the same `manifest.register` call or elsewhere in `init()`, untouched. "It logs one `info` line at boot naming the option" — it does. "The default is unchanged ... still refused" — pin 2, pin 3. "opens the synthesized default layout, without the Members / Invitations / Teams tabs" — the platform's synthesized default record page is the documented fallback "used when no page is assigned" (`packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts`, `content/docs/ui/pages.mdx`); the organization page's own header says its un-overridden slots fall through to it; `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/identity-auth.json` records what a grader sees when this page is absent (Details plus a stacked Related strip, "the synthesized default"). The rendering itself is objectui's and not read here; the repository's own contract text is consistent with the sentence. The README entry sits under `## Configuration` as `### Shipping your own organization record page`; its example and three bullets restate the TSDoc and are true. `Check Changeset` is green on both runs.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Dev's deviations, all accepted.** `manifest.ts` untouched — verified, it declares no page list. Docs on the package README rather than `content/docs` — `content/docs` holds no options table for `AuthPlugin` (only prose on `hostSignInHandoff` in `self-hosting.mdx`), so the README is the page that lists the options; the docs-drift comment lists eight pages that merely name the `AuthPlugin` symbol, none documenting the page list — no action. `spec test:repo` measured pre-merge only — the diff touches nothing under `packages/spec` and CI runs it. Attribution and worktree notes — procedural, in order.
2. **The `DefaultRecordPageConflictError` remedy text (the dev's out-of-scope finding, "carrier: none").** Its message says "compose the deployment without the package that ships the other", which for a plugin-auth holder is not a remedy a host can take (auth is not removable); the narrower remedy is now the option. Fine to leave here: the dispatch fenced the #23206 refusal off, the message names the holder package and page so a reader lands on plugin-auth's docs, and migration entry 18's `replacement` already reads "compose the deployment without that package's page (host composition)", which the option realises. It should become a filed follow-up on the #23206 surface rather than a note: reword the clause to "without that package's page" (generic, naming no option and no tracker number). Not a FAIL condition.
3. **Reachability from the composition roots — not this claim's surface, worth a card.** `packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts` (`os serve`) and `plugin-dev`'s `DevPlugin` construct `AuthPlugin` from a fixed option set (secret, baseUrl, appName, providers, plugins) and do not forward `registerOrganizationRecordPage`, so an app package that ships its own `sys_organization` default record page under `os serve` is still refused at boot with no switch to set. Cloud composes its own kernel, so the p1 chain (objectstack-ai/cloud#2709 via #2773) is served by this PR; the `os serve` host remains the gap, and the generic remedy text in flag 2 is what such a host reads. Out of the claim's file surface; recommend the PM file it.
4. **Minor, non-blocking:** no pin for an explicit `undefined` key (see ① c).

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-23254-auth-org-page-option`
Reviewed-by: `session_012uFegdfR6K6uqvLzt7XsdZ`

**VERDICT: PASS**
